blocks.text: Every monster in Unwritten is a **corrupted page** — a drawing from the artist's book that Chaos twisted into hostile form. That's why they appear **flat and papery**: their two-dimensional look isn't a style choice — it's what they *are*. To defeat one is to **restore its page**.

items: **By biome** — each biome (Grassland, Snow, Desert, Volcanic, Corrupted) has its own family of monsters. See *World & Maps*.

**By level** — every monster has a level, exactly like you do. That single number is what makes it dangerous; there is no separate difficulty rating. Ordinary monsters and elites run from level 1 to 99, and the shadows from 105 to 170. Every place has its own creatures, most of them near one level with the odd weaker or stronger visitor, and a monster lives wherever it belongs — you will meet the same slime in field after field.

**By kind** — most monsters are ordinary. A few in each area are **elites**: stronger, and they keep calling ordinary monsters to their side. Stronger still are the fourteen **shadows**, one for each weapon, each with a name of its own and gear at the highest grade — they call elites, and they are meant to take a whole guild to bring down. Anything a summoner calls gives nothing when it dies, and vanishes when its summoner does.

**By element** — a monster's element grows stronger with its kind: ordinary monsters are **level 1**, elites **level 2**, shadows **level 3**. Where a monster lives says what it probably is: the plains are mostly Neutral, the forests and hills Earth, the sea and snow Water, the volcano Fire, and the dark lands overseas Poison, Holy, Dark, Ghost and Undead. The shadows between them carry all ten elements, and a converter only answers the four it comes in — Water, Earth, Fire and Wind (see *Combat Mechanics*).

**By size** — every monster has a size of its own, set by what it is: a mouse barely reaches your ankle, a raccoon your knee, a bear stands taller than you and a giant squid towers four times your height. Every size falls into one of three groups — **Small, Medium or Large**. A Medium monster stands about as tall as you; a Small one under two-thirds of your height, a Large one more than one and a half times it. A bigger monster also reaches further with its blows — and you reach it from further away. Most ordinary monsters are Small or Medium; most elites are Large; every shadow is exactly your size. The size group is also meant to interact with your weapon type (see *Combat Mechanics*).

blocks.text: A monster is not built from a different set of numbers than you are. It has the **same six stats**, grown by the **same formulas**, and — this is the part that matters — it gets the **same number of stat points its level allows**. A level 20 monster is carrying exactly what a level 20 player could have bought. Nothing is inflated behind the scenes and nothing is quietly weakened.

items: **It wears real equipment** — the same gear you can wear, in the same slots. A monster's strength is its level, its stats, and its kit.
**It can carry Ring investment** — scaling it on the same soft-cap curve yours uses. A monster with a Ring behind it is a genuinely different fight.
**Its stats are visible in its numbers** — a monster that hits hard has the attack to prove it. There is no hidden multiplier making things tougher.

blocks.text: Because a monster is built like a character, anything a skill can do to you it can do to a monster — and the reverse. A monster can be slowed, shielded, guarded, drained, or pulled off its feet just as you can.

A monster **keeps what it wears** — its gear dies with it, because gear is made, not taken off a corpse. What it gives up is **materials** and **consumables** — never coin. What falls lands on the ground where it died: for 10 seconds only the player who earned the kill can pick it up, then anyone can, and it vanishes after a minute if nobody does.

items: **Materials** — the metal, cloth and leather of the monster's own grade, which rises with its level, and now and then an **Ink** or a **Salt**. Elites drop far more, and rarer Inks and Salts; shadows more again. No stats of their own; they feed **Crafting & Recycling**.
**Consumables** — potions and food, now and then; a monster with an element also drops the **converters** of its own element.

blocks.text: A beaten monster sometimes turns back into the character the artist really drew on its page — about **3 kills in 20**, for ordinary monsters and elites; a shadow never does. The monster's own drops still fall. The character says a line — for its first 2 seconds an aura shows which kind it is: hearts for one that never fights, stars for an ally, a dark haze for a rebel — and it stays for 30 seconds, doing one of three things:

items: **Some never fight.** They thank you, stay a while and leave — and saving one is the only way to earn **gold**: the monster's own gold range, times more for the helpless (children, the old) and more again for the wealthy (the princess, nobles, sultans).
**Some fight beside you** against monsters and rebels, then say goodbye. You cannot hit them, and what they beat counts as yours.

**Some rebel.** Cured of Chaos but choosing to fight, they attack anyone nearby like a monster does. A rebel carries **more and rarer loot** — as if it were one kind stronger — and the experience of the monster it came from. An elite always turns into the same ninja, and every ninja rebels.
**Elites** are the strongest corrupted pages of an area, and they keep calling ordinary monsters to their side.
**The shadows** are the Fourteen Kashira, turned by the artist's fear — the strongest creatures in the world, levels 105 to 170, one for each weapon.
